This is one axial slice of a T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI (radiological convention: patient right on image left, anterior at top). It contains a fibrous soft-tissue tumor.

The left panel is the clean image; the right panel shows numbered marks. Choose the ONE mark that lies inside the tumor, as close to its centre as possible. End your reply with a final line exactly: ANSWER: <mark number>

content.thinking:
I'm looking at this axial leg/ankle slice and noticing a bright lobulated mass in the subcutaneous region near the anterior-right area, trying to map the marker coordinates back to the panel's bright blob location.

Checking other labeled points, I rule out the one landing in the fascia and confirm the mass marker as the best match for the bright mass.

content.text:
The bright, lobulated mass sits in the anterior-right subcutaneous region, roughly at x 140–280, y 130–220 in the left panel. Mark 635 lies at about (191, 169) in that panel's coordinates, which is inside that mass near its centre. Mark 633 falls outside it, in the bright strands to the right of the mass, so 635 is the best choice.

ANSWER: 635
